item.title: Judge Approves $117.5 Million Settlement in ‘Complex’ Comcast Data Breach Case
item.description: A federal judge has approved a $117.5 million data breach settlement against Comcast Cable Communications. The agreement represents one of the largest data breach settlement amounts and, with 31.7 million potential members, one of the largest classes in a data breach case. The case also represents one of the more complex data breach cases to date, according to Judge John Younge of the U.S.

item.title: Chronic Traumatic Brain Damage Widespread in Former NFL Athletes
item.description: Almost every former National Football League player who died between 2016 and 2021 and allowed their brains to be evaluated were found to have chronic traumatic encephalopathy, stark evidence of the toll repeated head impacts can take on athletes. Researchers obtained personal information and causes of death for 878 players who died during the five-year period, when brain donations were highest. Of the 235 athletes whose brains were subject to the postmortem neurological examination, 215 had confirmed CTE, according to findings published Tuesday in the British Medical Journal.

item.title: Backcountry Guide Company Faces $150K Fine After Deadly California Avalanche
item.description: California workplace safety officials have fined a guide company that was leading backcountry skiers down a mountain in February when an avalanche was triggered, killing nine members of the group in the deadliest avalanche in the state’s modern history. The largest fine, $81,000, was for “failing to correct the imminent hazard posed by traveling in avalanche terrain when the avalanche danger was rated high.” The agency issued the fines earlier this month. The nine people who died were part of a group of 15 backcountry skiers headed out on a three-day trek organized by Blackbird Mountain Guides into pristine wilderness near Frog Lake in California’s Sierra Nevada as a powerful winter storm moved into the state.

item.title: What We Know About the Door Handles That Triggered China’s Record Auto Recall
item.description: Electronic door handles of the kind that are at the center of China’s largest-ever vehicle recall have proliferated across the globe over the past decade, especially on electric vehicles. Tesla and eight other automakers said on Friday they will recall a total of about 4.3 million vehicles in China over concerns that their doors may be difficult to open in an emergency. Popularized by Tesla, the door handles are designed to sit flush to the body of the door, for a minimalist look that also reduces aerodynamic drag.

item.title: Florida Man Arrested for $206K Luxury Vehicle Insurance Fraud Scheme
item.description: A Florida man was arrested after fraudulently submitting 41 vehicle insurance applications on luxury vehicles that he never owned, according to an announcement yesterday by the state’s Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia. Arrested earlier this month, he faces the following charges: organized scheme to defraud, insurance fraud, grand theft, and fraudulent use of personal identification. The Department of Financial Services Criminal Investigations Division (CID) investigators discovered that the man, Adam Otrok, used counterfeit and fictitious personal identification information to submit vehicle insurance applications.

item.title: ILS and broader securitisation key to absorbing nat cat risk: Schroders Capital
item.description: The increasing need for capital to manage and mitigate natural hazard risk is creating strong opportunities for investors, according to Schroders Capital, who emphasises that by allocating to catastrophe risk through insurance-linked securities, broader securitisation, and other risk-transfer markets, investors can secure attractive returns by absorbing catastrophe risk when pricing reflects expected losses and required margin. As natural hazard risk continues to intensify, Schroders Capital notes that the capital markets are increasingly being recognised as not only being a mechanism for absorbing financial losses, but also as a key source of financing for adaptation and resiliency. “Given the insurance industry’s enabling role for other economic activities, that approach should be closer to the way insurance has assessed risk: probabilistically, distribution-based, and with explicit acknowledgement of uncertainty,” Schroders Capital said.

item.description: I look forward to working with him as we continue strengthening USAA, delivering for our members and positioning the Association for what comes next.” Melcher has spent nearly seven years on the USAA Board, most recently as Vice Chairman. item.title: MS Amlin adds Alex Jomaa and Monica Tigleanu to cyber team
item.description: MS Amlin, a global specialty commercial insurance and reinsurance provider and part of MS&AD, has appointed Alex Jomaa as Head of Cyber and Monica Tigleanu as Lead Underwriter. In the new role, Jomaa will report to Stuart Wood, Director of Casualty and Cyber, MS Amlin. MS Amlin began writing cyber treaty in 2024, and expanded into direct cyber insurance in 2025 through a small number of strategic coverholder relationships.

item.title: Asia reinsurance market resilient as abundant capacity softens rates: AM Best
item.description: The Asian reinsurance market experienced abundant capacity, sliding rates, and over-placement during the 2026 renewal season, mirroring the same broad theme seen across the global reinsurance market, AM Best noted in a recent report. While this capacity has not materially disrupted market dynamics, early activity has been observed primarily in facultative and specialty lines, AM Best noted. Despite downward pricing pressure, cedents maintained largely stable deductibles, using ceded premium savings to buy up higher-layered limits and back emerging lines with growing risk appetites, according to AM Best’s AsiaFocus: Resilience Through Transformation report.

item.title: Missouri Contractor Sentenced for Fraud Scheme
item.description: Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway announced that a contractor has pled guilty to defrauding consumers through his residential contracting business. As part of his guilty plea, Matlock was sentenced to four years in prison on the deceptive business practices conviction and five years on the stealing conviction. Matlock, owner of Matlock Construction, pled guilty on August 17 to one felony count of deceptive business practices and one felony count of stealing.

item.title: People Moves: Alacrity Solutions Promotes Boyd to COO
item.description: Alacrity Solutions Group LLC , headquartered in Fishers, Indiana, promoted Lee Boyd to chief operating officer (COO). Backed by over two decades of experience in the insurance industry, Boyd joined Alacrity in 2021 and has held the roles of vice president of TPA Operations and, most recently, president of claims operations. As COO, Boyd oversees Alacrity’s operational strategy across claims and business functions, working closely with the executive leadership team to drive efficiency, scale technology initiatives, and support the company’s long-term strategic objectives.

item.title: Google Expands Gemini Enterprise AI Platform for Law Firms, Lawyers
item.description: Alphabet’s Google on Tuesday expanded its Gemini Enterprise artificial intelligence platform with new tools for lawyers and law firms, accelerating a race among technology companies to meet legal sector demand for AI. The company said its Gemini Enterprise for Legal would help law firms use AI to manage routine and complex work to allow lawyers to focus on higher-value services , while keeping their data secure and confidential. The new plug-in for Gemini Enterprise includes integration with legal software and data platforms and a stable of AI agents that Google said can handle specialized legal and administrative functions without significant human oversight.

item.title: $900m partnership: Sun Life and Wilton Re to launch Windsor Life Re reinsurer
item.description: As part of the deal, Wilton Re will establish Windsor Life Re, a US and Bermuda-domiciled reinsurer supporting growth of Wilton Re’s core in-force life and annuity block origination in the US. Sun Life Financial and Wilton Re have entered into a definitive agreement to establish a strategic reinsurance and asset management partnership, combining Wilton Re’s liability management expertise with Sun Life’s insurance and asset management capabilities. Under the terms of the agreement, Windsor Life Re will reinsure from Wilton Re an initial in-force block of approximately $1.7bn, with future business ceded by Wilton Re on a quota share basis.

item.title: ANV to acquire vehicle warranty MGA Car Care Plan from AmTrust
item.description: Insurance intermediary platform ANV Group Holdings has agreed to acquire UK-based vehicle warranty MGA Car Care Plan from AmTrust Financial Services. Founded in 1976, Car Care Plan provides vehicle warranties, asset protection products, and after-sales administration to more than 30 automakers and over 2,500 dealers. The transaction also includes Car Care Plan’s overseas subsidiaries in the US, Europe, Turkey, and China, as well as Dent Wizard Ventures, a UK provider of mobile bodywork, paint, and alloy-wheel repair services.

item.title: AUB Group international profit jumps 19.6% as UK retail platform scales
item.description: AUB Group’s International division was the standout performer in the group’s FY26 results, released to the Australian Securities Exchange today, lifting underlying net profit before tax 19.6% to A$124.5m and expanding EBIT margin by 410 basis points to 27.6%. The division houses Lloyd’s wholesale broker Tysers and the group’s expanding UK retail operations. At group level, AUB reported underlying net profit after tax of A$224.6m, up 12.2%, on revenue of A$1,596.6m.

item.title: Fuse Launches Terminal, Bloomberg for Commercial Insurance
item.description: New York, NY, August 25, 2026 — Fuse, the AI-powered market intelligence platform for commercial insurance, today announced the general availability of Fuse Terminal , a single-screen professional workspace that brings the entire Fuse platform — and the market it describes — to one keyboard-first surface. Two years in development, Terminal delivers the most real-time view of the commercial insurance market ever surfaced, and the closest thing to a Bloomberg Terminal the industry has ever had: one instrument-level view of the market, a short typeable address for every question, and — for the first time in any market terminal — answers written from the filing record itself. Commercial insurance never had that record — so we spent two years building it, and then we put a terminal on top,” said Sean Bourgeois, Founder & CEO of Fuse.

item.title: Sun Life and Wilton Re announce partnership
item.description: Sun Life Financial and Wilton Re have entered into a definitive agreement to establish a strategic reinsurance and asset management partnership. This partnership will combine Wilton Re’s liability management expertise with Sun Life’s insurance and asset management capabilities. The partnership is expected to deploy approximately $900 million of capital, anchored by strategic capital commitments from Sun Life and Wilton Re, each contributing approximately one-third of the total equity capitalization.

item.title: Obie partners with RentSpree
item.description: Obie, a provider of insurance solutions for landlords and real estate investors, announced a new collaboration with rental management software provider RentSpree. As part of the partnership, RentSpree users will be able to access Obie’s landlord insurance experience directly within the platform. “Working with Obie represents exactly what we set out to build at RentSpree: a comprehensive platform that simplifies every aspect of the rental lifecycle for landlords and agents.

item.title: Las pérdidas aseguradas por catástrofes en el primer semestre, en su nivel más bajo desde 2020
item.description: Swiss Re Institute estima las pérdidas aseguradas por catástrofes naturales en el primer semestre de 2026 en 42.000 millones de dólares, el nivel más bajo desde el primer semestre de 2020 y un 16% inferior a la media decenal.

item.title: LMIC Launches ISI AI for Submission Ingestion, Achieving 98%+ Accuracy
item.description: Go-live advances trusted submission intake workflows for professional liability underwriting Toronto, Ontario and Los Angeles, California – August 25 – ISI announced that Lawyers’ Mutual Insurance Company (LMIC) has successfully integrated ISI AI into its submission processing workflow. With the ISI AI Submission Agent now in production, LMIC’s underwriting team can access more complete, organized submission information earlier in the review process. Since going live, ISI AI now creates 67% of LMIC’s new business quotes with a 98%+ extraction accuracy rate prior to human involvement.

item.title: Why Bootstrapped Businesses Are More Relevant Than Ever
item.description: The more common path is bootstrapped or self-funded: Start with an existing customer problem and get paid more than it costs to solve it. The path may take longer than the VC “go big or go home” approach, but many small companies scale into middle market businesses, and a few of the best find their way to market leadership, even in tech. For every VC-backed startup, there are hundreds of bootstrapped founders building profitable businesses without any outside investment.

item.title: Inside The Private-Market Divide: EquityZen’s Phil Haslett On AI, SaaS And Secondaries
item.description: Phil Haslett , who co-founded EquityZen and serves as its chief strategy officer, has had a front-row seat to the secondary market’s evolution. As startups stay private longer, the market for buying and selling shares in venture-backed companies before they go public has become increasingly active — and heated. EquityZen has been operating in that market since 2013.

item.title: Alternative reinsurance capital and ILS market growth forecast for 2027: Fitch
item.description: Fitch Ratings anticipates the growth of the alternative reinsurance capital and insurance-linked securities (ILS) market will continue in 2027, as risk-adjusted returns remain attractive to investors and sponsor demand for capacity remains high, despite the backdrop of reinsurance rate softening. “Fitch expects strong alternative reinsurance capital market growth and attractive risk-adjusted returns into 2027, with investor supply and sponsor demand well balanced,” the rating agency said. One of the big questions for the continued growth potential of ILS and alternative capital is how long discipline holds in the market and for now Fitch feels that all-important T&Cs in reinsurance are being sustained.

item.title: AM Best expects UK captive insurance regime to compare well with established domiciles
item.description: The UK insurance regulator’s recent consultation paper on a bespoke regulatory framework for single-parent insurance captives is expected to create a captive regime that compares well with other established captive domiciles, according to AM Best. The regime aims to enhance the UK’s insurance market proposition by creating an internationally competitive market for captives while maintaining appropriate safeguards through PRA and FCA oversight. AM Best expects the flexible capital requirement framework to give the UK a competitive proposition.

item.title: Fuse introduces AI-powered commercial insurance market intelligence via new Terminal platform
item.description: Fuse, an AI-powered market intelligence company focused on commercial insurance, has launched Fuse Terminal, a new workspace designed to give insurance professionals access to market intelligence, analysis and underlying filing information through a single interface. Terminal has been developed over two years to provide a more consolidated way of assessing the commercial insurance market. Fuse said one of Terminal’s principal features is ASK, an AI-powered analyst that allows users to submit questions in natural language from the platform’s command line.

item.title: Aviva adds terrorism cover as standard in digital SME policies, citing Pool Re scheme
item.description: British insurer Aviva has added terrorism cover as standard to selected digitally traded commercial products for eligible small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) customers in Great Britain, with the insurer citing the recent scheme launched by the UK’s terrorism reinsurer Pool Re as helping them expand coverage in this way. Terrorism reinsurance rates available through the scheme have been reduced by up to 90% for the majority of policies, helping minimise the cost of including the cover as part of the overall premium. It follows the launch of Pool Re’s SME Incentive Scheme, an initiative designed to make terrorism protection more accessible and simplify broker-client conversations for SMEs.

item.title: New Zealand Insurance Industry Failing to Meet Māori Needs, Market Watchdog Says
item.description: New Zealand’s insurance industry is failing to consistently meet the needs of Māori, with affordability barriers and difficulties insuring collectively owned land leaving them less likely to have cover, according to a study by the market watchdog. “Participants also raised concerns about valuation, replacement costs and whether insurance products adequately reflect actual risk and cultural and intergenerational value.” The FMA oversees New Zealand’s financial markets and has identified significant knowledge gaps in the insurance sector about the experiences of Māori consumers and providers. The Financial Markets Authority research published Tuesday in Wellington found that 17% of the more than 950 Māori who participated in the study experienced problems with insurance in the last two years, which is almost twice the rate found in a similar survey of the general population.

item.title: Europe’s Record Heat Is Splitting Stock Winners From Losers
item.description: Even as Europe’s heat wave finally breaks, money managers say they’re still coming to terms with how climate change will affect their portfolios. Pictet Asset Management’s Katie Self says her firm has been fielding calls from clients about the risks and opportunities posed by the extreme heat. Nuveen says Europe’s drought will soon start affecting corporate credit spreads.

item.title: China’s Hackers Use DeepSeek for Attacks, Researchers Say
item.description: Chinese hackers are ramping up attacks after integrating DeepSeek and other open-source artificial intelligence models into their operations, highlighting attackers’ ability to leverage basic AI tools to hit targets abroad. Researchers said it wasn’t always possible to identify the AI model they used, but in general DeepSeek’s offerings are popular with hackers in the country because of its high performance and ability to be customized. While other models produced in the country are more powerful – including Moonshot’s breakout Kimi K3 model – hackers are drawn to DeepSeek’s relatively lax cybersecurity barriers and low cost of running, researchers said.

BBVA also offers travel-related benefits including cashback and no foreign exchange fees on card purchases. The partnership extends Chubb’s strategy of distributing travel insurance through financial institutions, airlines and travel platforms.

item.title: Solace Care raises €2.1 million
item.description: Stockholm-based Solace Care has raised €2.1 million in pre-seed funding to expand its digital legacy-planning and bereavement-support platform. Founded in January 2025, Solace Care offers services before and after a policyholder’s death. According to Solace Care, it surpassed 25,000 covered lives during its first year and currently serves Sweden, Finland and Norway.

item.title: Amazon’s New Order Confirmation Emails Seen Boosting Phishing Risk
item.description: In recent weeks, Amazon customers on TikTok and Reddit have also wondered why product names and images were replaced with labels such as “Household item” or “Essentials item” in order confirmation emails. “If anything, it increases risk.” Phishing attacks often mirror official emails and trick people into clicking on a bogus link that might contain malware or request login credentials. Vishwanath says Amazon’s new confirmation emails could encourage users to click on links without verifying who sent them.

item.title: Kentucky High Court Recalculates Employer Attorney Fees, Recovery in Subrogation
item.description: And an employer’s share of attorney fees must be deducted from the amount available from subrogation—not from the full settlement amount in a worker injury suit, the Kentucky Supreme Court decided in separate cases last week. The ALJ then subtracted the employer’s share of attorney fees in the suit against the vendor, leaving some $117,000 available for recovery in subrogation. Kentucky law bars injured workers from collecting duplicate benefits from the employer and a third party, and allows employers to seek recovery of benefits through subrogation.

item.title: Nuclear Verdicts Go Boom, Increase 40.7% in 2025
item.description: Verdicts like this against corporate defendants have come to be known as nuclear verdicts, and the total from 2025—a 40.7% increase over 2024—is the highest Marathon has seen since 2009. So-called “nuclear” verdicts did not subside in 2025. Product liability cases resulted in 29 nuclear verdicts totaling $12 billion in 2025.
